subject.title: feat(gateway): continue trusted HTTP trace context

question: Should Gateway accept W3C trace context from the existing trusted-proxy boundary for HTTP requests, with proxy-side header sanitization as the operator contract?
rationale: This is a new externally observable core Gateway capability and a deliberate trust-boundary extension; tests can validate mechanics but cannot establish whether this is the intended permanent product contract.

options.title: Accept the HTTP-only trusted-proxy contract
options.body: Keep the PR scoped to direct trusted peers, require proxy header sanitization, and defer WebSocket, tracestate, and baggage propagation.

options.title: Require a narrower owner design
options.body: Pause this PR until diagnostics and Gateway owners define whether inbound propagation belongs in core and what additional context fields, if any, are supported.

options.title: Decline inbound propagation
options.body: Retain fresh Gateway request traces and direct external orchestrators to correlate runs through existing diagnostics outside the Gateway header boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept the HTTP-only trusted-proxy contract
recommendation.body: Keep the PR scoped to direct trusted peers, require proxy header sanitization, and defer WebSocket, tracestate, and baggage propagation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current trace-context and OpenTelemetry design history most closely overlaps the permanent propagation contract.
